tests.exercises: The 1_EFT_GR deck exercises GR scalar and tensor evolution in equations.f90 and emits transfer, matter-power and CMB spectra. get_vector_cls=F: initialv/derivsv/outputv are owned without direct coverage.
tests.why: This is the official GR baseline for the selected scalar and tensor paths. Fixed ODE inputs and tabulated observables support pointwise comparison; byte-identical repeatability was tested only for 2_PEFT_Omega_const_1.ini, not this GR deck.

tests.exercises: All seven 2_PEFT_Omega decks force constant, exponential, linear, and power-law Omega couplings through the modified scalar perturbation system.
tests.why: These official decks cover the distinct Omega parametrization branches entering the modified perturbation equations. Their deterministic ODE trajectories and tabulated observables support pointwise comparison.

tests.exercises: All 21 2_PEFT_gamma decks cover the gamma1 and gamma3-gamma6 constant, exponential, linear, and power-law perturbation couplings.
tests.why: The gamma family is the broadest official branch coverage of the EFT-modified scalar system and would expose missing or incorrect coupling terms. Fixed ODE inputs support pointwise comparison; repeat-run byte identity has only been measured for 2_PEFT_Omega_const_1.ini.

tests.exercises: The two 2_PEFT_wDE decks exercise LCDM and wCDM background histories as inputs to the EFT perturbation evolution.
tests.why: This official pair tests that the perturbation system remains correct across the two supported dark-energy histories. Its fixed ODE solve and printed outputs make pointwise comparison suitable.

tests.exercises: All seven 3_RPH decks drive kineticity, braiding, Planck-mass, and tensor alpha-basis combinations through the scalar perturbation equations.
tests.why: The alpha-basis decks cover a numerically sensitive perturbation interface and showed the largest measured cross-machine lensed-spectrum spread. The evolution is still deterministic, so pointwise comparison with calibrated near-zero handling is proposed.

tests.exercises: All four 4_Des_F_R decks feed designer f(R) solutions on LCDM and wCDM backgrounds into the modified perturbation evolution.
tests.why: The official f(R) cases supply distinct designer solutions to the same linear evolution path and would expose an incorrect coupling or initial condition. Pointwise comparison fits the deterministic solver.

tests.exercises: All eight 4_Des_mc5e decks cover CPL, Taylor, turning-point, and wCDM designer quintessence histories coupled to perturbations.
tests.why: This family covers four independent designer-history branches and their paired parameters while grading the resulting transfer and spectra tables. The fixed ODE calculation supports pointwise comparison; only 2_PEFT_Omega_const_1.ini has repeat-run byte-identity evidence.

tests.exercises: All seven 5_Horava decks exercise solar-system and eta branches of the full-mapping model through linear perturbation evolution.
tests.why: The Horava decks force model-specific coefficients into the owned evolution code across seven official parameter regimes. Their reproducible tables make pointwise comparison appropriate.

tests.exercises: The six 5_Kmouflage and 5_Kmimic decks drive both screening-model branches through the scalar perturbation system.
tests.why: These official screening-model cases cover two related but distinct coefficient paths and grade their transfer, matter-power, and spectra consequences. Pointwise comparison matches the deterministic computation.

tests.exercises: Five quintessence potential decks plus the scaling-cubic Galileon deck exercise scalar-field initial conditions and evolution across six model forms.
tests.why: The family spans several scalar potentials and a Galileon branch, giving official coverage of materially different source terms in the owned evolution file. The fixed solver path supports pointwise comparison.

tests.exercises: The ADE deck and three 5_hdsk_TG decks exercise the full covariant Horndeski coefficient path and its costly per-k modified evolution.
tests.why: This is the strongest official end-to-end test of the acceleration target: it drives the full Horndeski coefficient machinery through the per-k ODE system and grades transfer, power, and spectra tables. The solve is deterministic, so pointwise comparison is proposed.
